title: HostedAPI latency lattice fallout — field notes and mitigation sketch
summary: Short-lived but severe p99/p999 latency and elevated 5xx for streaming connections. High skews on prefix-heavy workloads caused KV cache eviction cascades and scheduler coalescing to fall back to serialized execution. Result: client-visible timeouts and partial stream fragments. This doc captures quick forensic notes, actions taken during the event, and a first-pass runbook update proposal.
timeline:
2029-06-01 04:12: alert: synthetic p99 spike detected for hostedapi-us-west on per-route dashboard
2029-06-01 04:13: pager: SRE on-call paged for p99 > 2s + 5xx ratio > 1% across streaming routes
2029-06-01 04:14: oncall (Ava) triaged: confirmed elevated TCP connections and stream reconnects from edge
2029-06-01 04:16: SRE, serving-runtime, and edge teams joined bridge; correlating telemetry showed a sudden increase in KV-cache miss rate and lock contention in midchain
2029-06-01 04:20: applied emergency increase of KV cache size on a small subset of nodes (canary) — no immediate improvement; p99 still rising
2029-06-01 04:27: observed scheduler coalescer entering a serialized fallback path under headroom pressure (new flags from recent rollout) — requests that normally batch concurrently were being scheduled sequentially
2029-06-01 04:30: rolled back recent coalescer config flip (gate opened on 2029-05-28) in edge and runtime to restore previous behavior; slight improvement in tail latency after 4-6 minutes
2029-06-01 04:38: still saw intermittent stream fragments and 5xx spikes; traced representative session — client resumed after reconnect but with incomplete stream frames
2029-06-01 04:45: identified midchain eviction cascade triggered by uneven prefix distribution (a few customer prefixes generated disproportionate KV churn); turned on temporary prefix-affinity throttle for top 0.5% prefixes
2029-06-01 04:50: p99 decreased to near-normal for most routes; streaming 5xx rate dropped but not fully stabilized
2029-06-01 05:02: incident declared contained; continue monitoring. Bridge stood down with oncall watch and follow-ups assigned.
observations: The event surface looked like a compound failure: a configuration change to the coalescer scheduler reduced concurrency headroom in certain traffic shapes; this exposed an existing weakness in prefix distribution which caused KV cache churn and lock contention. The cache churn amplified scheduling pressure which pushed the runtime down fallback paths that serialized work and increased tail latencies. Streaming fragmentation/5xx were a downstream symptom when connections hit timeouts during serialized scheduling and reconnection churn. Not a single root bug but a brittle interaction between recent config rollout + uneven workload distribution + insufficient early warning for KV-lease thrash.
root_cause: Interaction bug: recent coalescer gating change (config flip deployed 2029-05-28) reduced allowance for concurrent batching under transient headroom pressure. For prefix-skewed workloads this caused rapid KV-cache eviction/lease churn in midchain; eviction-induced KV locks blocked worker threads and pushed scheduler to serialized fallback. Streaming subsystem timed out on in-flight frames during serialization, producing 5xx and client reconnections.
contributing_factors: Recent coalescer config change reduced concurrency headroom
High prefix skew from a small set of tenants amplified KV churn
KV cache eviction policy lacks graceful backoff once churn rate increases
Insufficient early telemetry on KV lease acquisition latency and lock contention
Rollout gating did not include a slow-burn canary for high-prefix-skew traffic
mitigations_deployed: Rolled back coalescer config flip in edge + runtime (2029-06-01 04:30)
Temporarily increased KV cache size and connection headroom on targeted nodes (canary) to blunt eviction cascade
Applied prefix-affinity throttle to top 0.5% prefixes to reduce churn (04:45)
Extended streaming connection timeouts for affected routes to avoid premature 5xx during transient scheduling (short-term only)
Enabled more verbose KV-lease and scheduler tracing during the containment window
follow_up_actions: SRE + Serving: add a histogram metric for KV-lease acquisition latency and per-prefix eviction rate (owner: Liam; ETA: 2 weeks)
Serving: implement graceful degrade for cache eviction (soft-backoff) to prevent lockstorms under churn (owner: Sofia; ETA: 3 weeks)
Edge: add rollout canary strategy that targets a mix of high-skew prefixes before global flip (owner: Ravi; ETA: 1 week)
Product: communicate to top affected customers with a summary and compensating measures (owner: Maya; ETA: 3 business days)
Runbook: add automated mitigation steps (prefix throttle, rollback gate, cache bump) and run a tabletop exercise (owner: Ava; ETA: 1 week)
Post-incident follow-up postmortem doc with trace-level artifacts and flamegraphs (owner: team; ETA: 1 week)
Consider circuit-breaker at edge level to detect and quarantine prefix storms (discuss in architecture review; owner: arch-team; ETA: next planning cycle)
runbook_updates: Proposed runbook additions: 1) Detect: add alert for per-prefix eviction rate > 200 evictions/min + KV-lease-latency > 50ms; 2) Mitigate: scripted steps for temporary prefix-affinity throttle, fast rollback of coalescer flag, and controlled KV cache bump with canary; 3) Post-containment: enable verbose tracing and collect representative session traces; 4) Postmortem checklist including communication templates for customers and SRE post-incident review calendar.
notes_to_oncall: If you see a sudden spike in p99 with correlated increases in kv-lease-latency and per-prefix eviction rate: 1) immediately flip coalescer gate back to previous value and validate bootstrap on small canary nodes; 2) if eviction rate remains high, apply prefix-affinity throttle to top offending prefixes; 3) do not increase global cache size without canarying the change — prefer per-pool canary bumps; 4) escalate to serving-runtime lead if serialized scheduling paths are observed in traces; 5) document timestamps and take heap/profile snapshots for later analysis.
